steps.title: The friendly new customer
steps.prompt:
So far we only READ. INSERT ADDS a row - like a guest book getting a new signature.
You name the columns, then list the VALUES in the same order.
steps.task: Try typing: INSERT INTO customers (name, email, city, created_at) VALUES ('Amina', 'amina@shop.ma', 'Rabat', '2026-05-01');
hints: Start with INSERT INTO customers.
List the columns you're filling in brackets.
VALUES holds the facts, in the same order.
Write the full INSERT with 'Amina' first.
steps.expected_sql: INSERT INTO customers (name, email, city, created_at) VALUES ('Amina', 'amina@shop.ma', 'Rabat', '2026-05-01');
steps.memory_trick: INSERT INTO = 'add to…', VALUES = 'these are the facts'.

steps.title: Add a product
steps.prompt:
Practice the muscle memory - add a fresh jar of argan oil:
INSERT INTO products (name, category_id, supplier_id, price, stock, created_at) VALUES ('Argan Oil 250ml', 2, 1, 149.99, 12, '2026-05-02');
steps.task: Try typing the INSERT for the argan oil.
hints: It's an INSERT INTO products query.
Fill the columns: name, category_id, supplier_id, price, stock, created_at.
The values come in brackets after VALUES.
Watch the quotes around text and the commas between values.
steps.expected_sql: INSERT INTO products (name, category_id, supplier_id, price, stock, created_at) VALUES ('Argan Oil 250ml', 2, 1, 149.99, 12, '2026-05-02');
steps.memory_trick: Column list and value list must march in the same order.

steps.title: Fill the values
steps.prompt:
Your turn to invent one fact at a time. Fill the blanks:
INSERT INTO customers (name, city) VALUES (___, ___);
steps.task: Add the customer Yasmine from Casablanca.
hints: Two columns, two values.
Text needs single quotes.
Name comes first, then city.
Fill: 'Yasmine', 'Casablanca'.
steps.memory_trick: Every value keeps its own quote-needing or bare nature.

steps.title: Predict the missing email
steps.prompt:
This INSERT fills only name and city:
INSERT INTO customers (name, city) VALUES ('Omar', 'Tangier');
The email column is left out. The table lets email be missing (it's nullable).
What value fills the empty email?
steps.task: What's the special word for 'this value is missing'?
hints: You've met this word in the COUNT lesson.
It's the word for 'no value there'.
Four letters, starts with n.
Answer: NULL.
steps.memory_trick: NULL = the honest way to say 'nothing here'.

steps.title: Add and check
steps.task: Run the INSERT, then the SELECT.
hints: Two statements, separated by a new line.
First add Yasmine.
Then look her up with WHERE name = 'Yasmine'.
Run INSERT first and SELECT second.
steps.expected_sql:
INSERT INTO customers (name, city) VALUES ('Yasmine', 'Casablanca');
SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE name = 'Yasmine';
